“The loop is sacred”

The core loop is the privileged path: it turns model output into local actions. It stays focused on execution contracts and lifecycle correctness. Capabilities with their own policy, dependency, or product tradeoff live outside it as extensions or host wiring.

THE PRACTICAL RESULT

Adding MCP, web tools, retries, output truncation, event streaming, or a terminal UI does not require those concerns to become inseparable from the dispatcher’s hot path.

Parallel, deterministic work

Independent tools should not wait for one another. But concurrency must not make a model’s next step ambiguous. The dispatcher runs work in parallel when allowed, then restores the model-visible result order and original call/result pairing.

ClassificationGuarantee
ParallelRuns alongside other eligible work; this is the default.
SerialRuns exclusively; no other tool executes at the same time.
Keyed(key)Calls sharing a key serialize in call order; unrelated keys can still run concurrently.

File writes use keyed scheduling by path: two writes to one file stay ordered, while separate files need not wait for each other.

Policy and observability

ToolPolicy can allow, deny, or apply a custom decision before execution. EventStream exposes typed lifecycle events suitable for a UI or NDJSON stream. Truncation, retries, and usage metering attach to the hooks they need rather than becoming hidden behavior inside every tool.

For users, that design shows up as predictable approvals, plan-mode enforcement, readable activity rails, recoverable large output, and the option to extend the agent without forking the kernel.
